stories.h: Oil firm Nembe disputes EFCC narrative on recovered pipeline fees
stories.e: Nembe Exploration and Production Company, formerly Aiteo, has pushed back on reports about funds the EFCC recovered from third-party oil operators, insisting the money represents unpaid pipeline transportation fees long owed to its joint venture with NNPCL, not a debt the company itself owes. The firm said years of crude theft, pipeline vandalism and COVID-19 disruptions had made it difficult to reconcile the volumes involved, and that it had sought payment directly before the EFCC intervened. It denied any wrongdoing and said a separate stamp duty matter tied to an earlier asset acquisition remains under review with the relevant authorities.

stories.h: INEC sets 28 November mock accreditation to test new election safeguards
stories.e: The Independent National Electoral Commission has scheduled a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise for 28 November to test an upgraded Bimodal Voter Accreditation System ahead of the 2027 general election. Chairman Joash Amupitan, speaking in London, said the commission has introduced a safeguard that blocks inaccurate polling-unit results from reaching its result-viewing portal, and has cut the maximum number of voters assigned to each device from 1,250 to 850.

stories.h: Anambra to recruit 200 health workers, warns against favouritism in hiring
stories.e: Anambra State's primary healthcare agency says it plans to recruit about 200 community health extension workers and at least 50 midwives drawn from the communities they will serve, as part of efforts to strengthen primary healthcare delivery. Officials used a workshop for ward committee members, run under the SPARK II programme, to warn against political favouritism in the recruitment process and to train participants to track patient feedback on maternal and child health services. Lawmakers at the event also raised concerns about facility heads who are frequently absent from their posts.

stories.h: INEC sets 28 November for nationwide mock accreditation ahead of 2027 polls
stories.e: The Independent National Electoral Commission has scheduled a nationwide mock accreditation exercise for 28 November to field-test the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System and other equipment before the February 2027 general election. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan said the exercise would help identify technical gaps, though the plan's scope has been constrained by budget limits.

stories.h: Court commits Maina's son to begin serving seven-year jail term
stories.e: A Nigerian court has ordered Faisal Maina, son of former pension reform taskforce chairman Abdulrasheed Maina, to be committed to prison to begin serving a seven-year sentence over the multi-billion-naira pension fraud scandal. The term follows an earlier appellate ruling that had halved his original 14-year sentence.

stories.h: EFCC arraigns businessman over alleged £122,000 investment fraud
stories.e: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission arraigned businessman Ashley Oshin before a Lagos State High Court over an alleged £122,000 investment fraud dating back to 2009. He is accused of promising two investors a 40 per cent annual return through a fund he knew to be fraudulent, and he pleaded not guilty. The judge remanded him in a correctional centre and adjourned the matter to 18 November for trial and a bail hearing.

stories.h: FIJ journalist Daniel Ojukwu remanded in Kuje over SDG spending investigation
stories.e: A Federal High Court in Abuja remanded investigative journalist Daniel Ojukwu in Kuje Correctional Centre after he pleaded not guilty to 12 counts of cyberstalking and criminal defamation linked to his reporting on spending by the presidential SDG office. The case stems from Foundation for Investigative Journalism reports that questioned how funds were used under former aide Adejoke Orelope-Adefulire. His bail hearing was adjourned to 1 December, while press-freedom groups have condemned the prosecution as an attempt to intimidate reporters covering public spending.

stories.h: Makinde campaign group demands probe of Tinubu's ₦11.2trn crude-backed loans
stories.e: A campaign organisation backing Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde's presidential bid has called for an open investigation into federal plans to pledge about 340 million barrels of future crude output to secure roughly ₦11.2 trillion in loans. The group wants the government to disclose the lenders, interest rates, fees and repayment terms behind four financing arrangements, warning that mortgaging future oil revenue could leave Nigeria worse off if prices rise. It has urged the National Assembly to hold a public hearing and President Tinubu to explain the deals.

stories.h: EFCC witness alleges Emefiele used associates to acquire properties
stories.e: An investigator testifying for the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission told a Nigerian court that former Central Bank governor Godwin Emefiele used associates to acquire properties in Lagos, Delta, Ogun and Abuja states, as part of the ongoing corruption trial against him. The testimony adds to the EFCC's long-running effort to trace and recover assets allegedly linked to Emefiele since his 2023 arrest.

stories.h: Media coalition demands release of detained journalist Daniel Ojukwu
stories.e: A coalition of 17 Nigerian civil society and media groups, including BudgIT, SERAP and the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development, has condemned a Federal High Court order remanding Foundation for Investigative Journalism reporter Daniel Ojukwu at Kuje Correctional Centre. He faces a 12-count charge linked to 2023 reports questioning spending on SDG classroom projects by a presidential aide's office, and the coalition says denying him continued bail amounts to an attack on press freedom. His bail hearing has been fixed for 1 December 2026.

stories.h: Court jails Mainas son for seven years over pension fraud laundering
stories.e: The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered that Faisal Maina, son of jailed former pension boss Abdulrasheed Maina, be moved to a correctional centre to serve a seven-year sentence. Justice James Omotosho granted an EFCC application to enforce the conviction after Maina fled trial in 2020 and was later re-arrested in Abuja in October. He was convicted in 2021 of laundering over N58 million in pension funds through a fictitious bank account.

stories.h: INEC says fake AI-generated photos found in voter register across 10 states
stories.e: Nigeria's electoral commission disclosed that officials in ten states had uploaded AI-generated images into the national voters' register, which have since been pulled down. INEC Commissioner Mohammed Kudu Haruna said the implicated staff have been identified and face disciplinary action, as the commission races to finalise an artificial-intelligence policy ahead of the 2027 polls. The episode has added to concerns over the integrity of the preliminary voter register.

stories.h: Senate summons NCC, MTN, Airtel and Globacom over dropped calls and airtime deductions
stories.e: The Senate's Committee on Communications, chaired by Ikra Bilbis, has summoned the Nigerian Communications Commission and operators MTN, Airtel, Globacom and T2 over persistent dropped calls and failed connections for which subscribers say they are still billed. Lawmakers want the committee to establish the scale of the financial losses to consumers and report back within four weeks. The move follows long-running complaints from Nigerians about poor network quality despite rising call charges.

stories.h: Tinubu asks House of Representatives to approve N10.79tn in fresh external borrowing
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has formally asked the House of Representatives to approve N10.79 trillion in external borrowing already authorised under the 2026 Appropriation Act, mainly through Eurobonds alongside concessional and commercial loans. The funds are meant to help plug the N31.4 trillion budget deficit and finance capital projects spanning infrastructure, defence, agriculture, health, power, transport and education. The request has been referred to the House committees on Aids, Loans and Debt Management, and Finance, for scrutiny.

stories.h: NULGE demands release of withheld Osun local government funds after strike
stories.e: The Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees has called on the federal and Osun State governments to urgently release funds withheld from the states local councils, blaming the dispute for a warning strike that ran from 8 to 11 November. The union said the standoff undermines the Supreme Courts affirmation of local government financial autonomy and described it as a threat to grassroots democracy rather than a mere labour dispute.

stories.h: Afenifere raises alarm over worsening kidnappings across South-West
stories.e: Pan-Yoruba group Afenifere has warned that insecurity is deepening across Nigerias South-West, citing a fresh wave of kidnappings in Ogun, Oyo and Osun states. It urged state governments and security agencies to act urgently to protect residents, saying parts of the region can no longer be considered safe.

stories.h: IGP cancels officers leave, restricts senior police movement ahead of 2027 polls
stories.e: Inspector-General Olatunji Disu has suspended leave for officers on election security duty and ordered commissioners of police to remain in their commands unless cleared by Force Headquarters. He warned that any officer found colluding with politicians to rig the 2027 elections would face disciplinary action.

stories.h: Ogoni leaders withhold consent for oil resumption, demand community congresses
stories.e: The Ogoni Dialogue Committee says it will not sign any memorandum of understanding on resuming oil exploration until communities across the four Ogoni local government areas endorse it through credible congresses. Leaders also want suspended confidence-building projects, including the abandoned Eleme stretch of the East-West Road, completed before any deal is accepted.

stories.h: Edo senator petitions Senate over Lagos demolition of constituents property
stories.e: Senator Joseph Ikpea has asked the Senate to intervene after a Lagos State task force reportedly demolished a constituents Ikoyi property despite a valid certificate of occupancy and without prior notice. Senate President Godswill Akpabio referred the petition to the Committee on Ethics for further investigation.

stories.h: INEC uncovers AI-generated photos in voters register, to discipline staff
stories.e: Nigeria's electoral commission says it detected artificial intelligence-generated photographs uploaded to the national voters register in roughly ten states and has identified the staff responsible. INEC Commissioner Mohammed Haruna said disciplinary action would follow and that a policy on AI misuse is being finalised ahead of the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Review: how 2027 Lagos governorship candidates fared in live debate
stories.e: An analysis of a recent live debate among four candidates for Lagos State's 2027 governorship race, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, Obafemi Hamzat, Funso Doherty and Adedeji Doherty, examined their answers on housing, transport, flooding and why Lagos remains wealthy on paper while many residents stay poor. Rhodes-Vivour and Hamzat were judged to have offered the most detailed plans, including housing targets and transport schemes, while Adedeji Doherty was assessed as the least prepared, declining to set a housing target. Several candidates were criticised for promising free services or large infrastructure programmes without explaining how they would be funded.

stories.h: INEC chairman Amupitan says his loyalty is solely to the constitution
stories.e: Facing renewed criticism over the commission's handling of pre-2027 election disputes, INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan said his allegiance is to the constitution and the will of Nigerians, not to any political interest. The remarks come amid opposition pressure over INEC's rulings on party primaries and candidate lists ahead of next year's polls.

stories.h: Federal High Court orders INEC to list Adebutu as Ogun PDP governorship candidate
stories.e: Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered INEC to publish Ladi Adebutu's name as the PDP's governorship candidate for Ogun State within 24 hours, ruling that the commission had no power to exclude a candidate properly nominated by his party. INEC had dropped Adebutu over an alleged register dispute, but the court found the party had complied with submission rules.

stories.h: Senate committee warns petroleum regulators against sabotaging government policy
stories.e: The Senate Committee on Petroleum Downstream, chaired by Kawu Sumaila, warned regulatory agencies in the oil and gas sector against undermining government policy, saying some agencies were failing to support the president's vision for the sector. The warning came as the committee cleared seven nominees for executive director roles at the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority.

stories.h: 2027 Politics Watch: political violence flares as ADC suffers legal setback
stories.e: A Premium Times politics roundup highlights rising political violence ahead of the 2027 elections alongside an internal legal setback for the opposition African Democratic Congress. The report forms part of ongoing coverage tracking party manoeuvring and unrest as campaigning for the 2027 polls intensifies.

stories.h: Federal government reviews 932 laws, scraps 269 obsolete enactments
stories.e: The federal government has completed a review of 932 existing laws and removed 269 obsolete enactments from the new Laws of the Federation of Nigeria. The exercise is intended to modernise the statute book and strip out redundant or conflicting legislation.

stories.h: INEC adds safeguard to block inaccurate results from IReV, sets mock poll for 28 November
stories.e: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan said the commission has built a technical safeguard that will stop inaccurate polling-unit results from reaching its public result-viewing portal, aiming to close gaps exposed during the 2023 elections. He announced that a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise will take place on 28 November to test the upgraded system before the 2027 general elections. The presidential and National Assembly polls are scheduled for 16 January 2027, with governorship elections to follow in February.

stories.h: Suspected thugs attack NDC town hall venue ahead of Obi's Lagos event
stories.e: Suspected thugs attacked the venue of a town hall meeting organised for Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate Peter Obi in Lagos, damaging vehicles ahead of the event. The incident drew swift condemnation from party figures, who called it an attempt to intimidate supporters and disrupt the party's campaign activities in the state.

stories.h: Dickson alleges plot to rig 2027 polls using fake security officers
stories.e: Nigeria Democratic Congress leader and Bayelsa West senator Seriake Dickson has alleged, in remarks to party youth and women leaders in Bayelsa State, that there are plans to manipulate the 2027 election and intimidate voters using impersonated security personnel. He urged INEC and security agencies to act impartially and called on supporters to resist any malpractice through lawful means rather than confrontation.

stories.h: Makinde explains decision to challenge Tinubu in 2027 presidential race
stories.e: Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, now the Allied Peoples Movement's presidential candidate, has published a newsletter explaining why he withdrew his backing for President Bola Tinubu ahead of the January 2027 election. He argues the government has stabilised the economy without translating the gains into jobs or living standards, and faults its handling of fuel subsidy removal and the weakening of opposition parties. Makinde says he would serve a single four-year term leading a transitional government of national unity.

stories.h: Thugs disrupt Peter Obis NDC town hall meeting in Lagos
stories.e: A town hall event for NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi in Lagos was disrupted when suspected thugs attacked attendees, damaging property and injuring some participants, according to eyewitnesses. The incident adds to a string of violent disruptions at opposition political gatherings ahead of the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: ADC lawyer says Justice Lifu's ruling does not nullify Atiku's 2027 presidential candidacy
stories.e: Lawyers for the African Democratic Congress have rejected claims that a Federal High Court ruling by Justice Peter Lifu, which declared the David Mark-led caretaker leadership of the party unlawful, also voids Atiku Abubakar's 2027 presidential candidacy. The party argues the judgment cannot override an earlier, still-standing ruling from a court of coordinate jurisdiction and says the matter has effectively been overtaken by events. The dispute is the latest round in a wider legal battle over control of the ADC ahead of next year's elections.

stories.h: ADC dismisses Tinubus 2027 manifesto as recycled, unfulfilled promises
stories.e: The African Democratic Congress has rejected President Bola Tinubus newly unveiled 2027-2031 manifesto, arguing it merely repackages 2023 campaign pledges on electricity, jobs, food prices and the naira that his government has failed to deliver. The opposition coalition said subsidy removal, tax rises and heavy borrowing have brought hardship without accountable results, and urged Nigerians to judge the ruling party on its record rather than fresh promises.

stories.h: Senate threatens to summon telecom operators and minister over poor service
stories.e: The Nigerian Senate has threatened to summon telecommunications operators and the Minister of Communications over persistent poor network quality and unexplained airtime deductions affecting subscribers nationwide. Lawmakers said regulators must act more forcefully to hold operators accountable and protect consumers from arbitrary charges.

stories.h: Uzodimma vows to keep APC senatorial ticket despite court ruling
stories.e: Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma has said he will not relinquish his All Progressives Congress senatorial ticket, despite a court judgment ordering INEC to recognise Rochas Okorocha as the party's candidate for Imo West instead. The dispute underlines ongoing tension within the APC over candidate selection ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.h: Tinubu seeks National Assembly approval for N10.8 trillion external loan
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has written to the House of Representatives seeking approval to implement a N10.8 trillion external borrowing plan, adding to Nigeria's already substantial public debt load. The request is likely to draw fresh scrutiny of the government's growing reliance on foreign loans amid rising debt-servicing costs.

stories.h: Tinubu launches ₦52,500 minimum pension and free healthcare scheme for retirees
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has launched a Minimum Pension Guarantee setting a ₦52,500 monthly floor for retirees under the Contributory Pension Scheme, more than two decades after the guarantee was first written into pension law. The government also unveiled PenCare, a healthcare programme for low-income pensioners, backed by a newly created ₦400 billion Pension Protection Fund expected to benefit over 173,000 retirees.

stories.h: Atiku's supporters protest in Abuja after court voids his candidacy
stories.e: Supporters of Atiku Abubakar protested in Abuja after a Federal High Court judgment declared his African Democratic Congress presidential nomination void, with the court also ruling the party's leadership committee and the primary that produced him as candidate illegal. Atiku has urged his supporters to remain calm, insisting his 2027 campaign will continue while the party challenges the ruling on appeal.

stories.h: INEC warns against 'Rig and Die' slogan ahead of 2027 general election
stories.e: INEC has cautioned that the slogan Rig and Die endangers electoral officials, voters and observers ahead of the 2027 general election, with commissioner Mohammed Kudu Haruna urging political leaders to discourage its use and journalists not to amplify it. Speaking through Enugu's resident electoral commissioner at a media forum, INEC said presiding and collation officers are especially vulnerable to attack, and pointed to the Electoral Act 2026 as the proper route for pursuing electoral offences rather than threats of violence. The commission also referenced vote-buying in Ekiti's governorship poll and false, AI-generated claims during the Osun election as warning signs for 2027.

stories.h: Wike defends N10m councillor reward as incentive, not vote-buying
stories.e: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike has defended his pledge to pay N10 million to each councillor who delivers their ward for President Tinubu in the 2027 elections, insisting it rewards political mobilisation rather than inducing voters, and comparing it to incentive payments for athletes. He made the promise during a Rainbow Coalition grassroots mobilisation event in Kwali Area Council and criticised journalists for conflating organiser incentives with vote-buying. Wike also said several FCT road and infrastructure projects would be completed by mid-December, ahead of the January 2027 polls.

stories.h: Bakers say high energy costs and loan rates have shut 40% of businesses
stories.e: The Premium Breadmakers Association of Nigeria says about 40 per cent of its members have closed in the past two years, squeezed by commercial lending rates of around 34 per cent and energy costs that now make up about half of production expenses. One member said her bakery's monthly diesel bill nearly doubled, to about N19 million, while bread profit margins have fallen below 30 per cent and bakers say they cannot pass rising costs on to customers. The association said it has not yet felt any relief from the Central Bank's recent interest rate cut, and is appealing to the federal government and the Bank of Industry for cheaper financing.

stories.h: FG signs Port Harcourt airport concession deal, pledges to protect workers
stories.e: The Federal Government has formally signed the concession agreement handing Port Harcourt International Airport to a private operator, following a similar deal earlier this year for Enugu's Akanu Ibiam Airport. Officials pledged to safeguard the interests of existing aviation workers, after unions had warned the concession could put jobs at risk.

stories.h: Deutsche Bank arranges $516m financing for Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway
stories.e: Deutsche Bank has secured $516.3 million in Shariah-compliant financing, backed by an ICIEC sovereign insurance policy, to fund the first phase of Nigeria's planned 1,290km Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway. The nine-year facility covers only the opening section of the route, with the rest of the project still to be financed.

stories.h: FG concessions Port Harcourt airport, assures workers of job security
stories.e: The federal government has handed Port Harcourt International Airport to a private concessionaire as part of its airport privatisation drive, while assuring existing staff that their jobs will be protected under the new arrangement. The move forms part of a wider push to improve infrastructure and efficiency at airports across the country.

stories.h: Staple food prices surge in Lagos markets, signalling fresh rise in food inflation
stories.e: A BusinessDay survey of Lagos's Mile 12 and Ketu markets found sharp October price rises for staples such as onions, maize and rice, with a 100kg bag of onions nearly quadrupling in price. Traders blamed higher transport and fuel costs, tight supply and festive-season stockpiling, while analysts expect the trend to push food inflation higher after September's rate of 19.59 per cent. The increases add to pressure on households already grappling with a high cost of living.

stories.h: S&P warns Nigeria's rising debt costs expose a shallow capital market
stories.e: A new S&P Global Institute report says Nigeria's public debt climbed to 38 per cent of GDP in 2025, up from 23 per cent a decade earlier, while interest payments now consume 24 per cent of government revenue. The agency argues genuine capital-market development needs more than growing bond issuance, pointing to thin private-sector credit and shallow pension and insurance markets as structural weaknesses still holding the country back.

stories.h: Nigeria hits OPEC oil quota for sixth straight month despite October dip in output
stories.e: Nigeria's crude output, excluding condensates, averaged about 1.51 million barrels per day in October 2026, roughly 101 per cent of its 1.5 million bpd OPEC quota, marking the sixth consecutive month the country has met its target even as overall output slipped 1.7 per cent month-on-month. The upstream regulator, NUPRC, attributed the sustained compliance to improved operational stability and more efficient crude evacuation. Dangote Group has projected fourth-quarter output could rise further, to about 1.72 million bpd.

stories.h: Marketers push back as FCCPC presses for lower petrol prices
stories.e: After consumer protection agency FCCPC noted that Brent crude had fallen from a September peak of $115 to below $90 a barrel and urged marketers to cut pump prices accordingly, marketer groups PETROAN and PEDAN said falling crude does not translate quickly into cheaper petrol. They cited existing higher-cost stock, the weak naira and lags in cargo pricing and depot delivery, and asked the FCCPC to engage them directly on how the downstream market works.

stories.h: Nigerias solid minerals revenue hits N101bn in nine months, says minister
stories.e: Solid minerals revenue collected between January and September 2026 reached about N101.11 billion, nearly double the same period last year, Mining Minister Dele Alake has announced. Royalties made up the bulk of the collections, which Alake credited to tighter enforcement and the formalisation of mining activity.

stories.h: Afreximbank, Development Bank of Nigeria sign $75m SME and creative-sector facility
stories.e: Afreximbank and the Development Bank of Nigeria have signed a $75 million facility, announced at CANEX WKND in Lagos, to expand lending to small businesses, including those in fashion, film and music. DBN will channel the funds through partner institutions, covering working capital, equipment purchases and export-readiness support.

stories.h: Naira falls to 10-month low of N1,430 to the dollar in black market
stories.e: The naira has slid to a 10-month low of N1,430 to the dollar in the parallel market, reflecting renewed pressure on Nigeria's currency despite ongoing central bank interventions. Analysts pointed to rising demand for foreign exchange and tighter global financing conditions as key drivers of the latest depreciation.

stories.h: S&P says rising energy costs and costly borrowing threaten Nigeria's economic recovery
stories.e: S&P Global Ratings has raised Nigeria's long-term foreign currency rating to B with a stable outlook, citing an improving naira and easing inflation, but warned that steep diesel price rises and expensive government borrowing could erode these gains. The agency estimated Nigeria's 2026 fiscal deficit at 4.4 per cent of GDP, with interest payments consuming over a fifth of government revenue.

stories.h: Oil prices fall below $90 as Middle East peace hopes grow
stories.e: Brent crude slipped below $90 a barrel for the first time since August after President Trump suggested the nearly nine-month US conflict with Iran could end soon, with US WTI trading below $85. The latest diplomatic push is being mediated by Qatar, though sticking points remain, including Iran's demand that the US lift its naval blockade and sanctions, and US demands that Iran stop attacking Strait of Hormuz shipping and make nuclear concessions. As a major oil exporter, Nigeria's revenue outlook is sensitive to these price swings, which have reversed sharply from a six-month high reached in late October.

stories.h: Dangote Refinery IPO draws N5.85trn in bids from nearly 3.8m applicants
stories.e: Dangote Petroleum Refinery's initial public offering attracted about N5.85 trillion in share applications from almost 3.8 million subscribers, well above its N2.15 trillion target, with investors applying for 11.15 billion shares against the 4.1 billion on offer at N525 each. Retail investors made up roughly 84 per cent of applicants but a small handful of large subscribers accounted for nearly half of the shares sought by value. The company reported nine-month revenue of $22.48 billion, up 144 per cent year-on-year, with final allotments still subject to regulatory approval.

stories.h: Nigerian air traffic controllers threaten strike over failing equipment
stories.e: Air traffic controllers in Nigeria have warned they may down tools over ageing and malfunctioning navigation equipment, which they say is putting flight safety at risk. The controllers are demanding urgent government investment in airport infrastructure rather than further delays. A strike would threaten significant disruption to domestic and international flights out of Nigerian airports.

stories.h: Makinde presents ₦1.1trn final budget, allocates ₦670bn to capital projects
stories.e: Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde presented a ₦1.1 trillion budget to the state assembly, his last as governor before the 2027 transition, with roughly ₦670 billion earmarked for capital projects. The administration framed the spending plan as a push to complete ongoing infrastructure before leaving office. Lawmakers are expected to scrutinise the allocations in the coming weeks before passage.

stories.h: Dangote Cement suspends planned London Stock Exchange listing
stories.e: Dangote Cement has called off its previously announced plan to list on the London Stock Exchange, without giving a definitive new timeline. The decision affects one of Africa's largest cement producers and comes amid broader volatility in Nigerian equities this week.

stories.h: Tinubu pledges single-digit inflation and 6% growth by 2031 if re-elected
stories.e: President Tinubu has promised that, if re-elected in 2027, his administration will cut inflation below 8 per cent, grow the economy by 6 per cent annually, and add 10,000 megawatts of electricity capacity by 2031. The pledges form part of his emerging economic agenda for a prospective second term.

stories.h: NGX stocks surge as Dangote Cement, First Holdco, Aradel ride FTSE upgrade
stories.e: Shares in Dangote Cement, First Holdco and Aradel Holdings have driven a sharp rally on the Nigerian Exchange, with the All-Share Index up roughly 58 to 60 per cent this year, after FTSE Russell restored Nigeria to Frontier Market status and named ten Nigerian stocks eligible for its frontier index series. Analysts have cautioned that some of the gains may prove volatile as investors begin booking profits.

stories.h: Nigeria's inflation projected to ease further to 13.99% in October
stories.e: BusinessDay's economic analysis projects that Nigeria's headline inflation eased to 13.99 per cent in October, which would mark a fifth consecutive monthly decline, following September's reading of 14.63 per cent. The outlook remains fragile, as rising fuel, transport and fertiliser costs could put renewed upward pressure on prices even as the broader disinflation trend continues.

stories.h: Nigerian stock market claws back N3.5trn pullback as Dangote listing nears
stories.e: The Nigerian Exchange has recovered most of a roughly N3.5 trillion sell-off that followed a late-October rally, with its All-Share Index rising 1.36 per cent in the week to 13 November as investors continued taking profits unevenly across sectors. Industrial goods stocks drove much of the rebound, climbing over 18 per cent, while banking, oil and gas, and consumer goods shares all lost ground over the same period. Analysts say the recovery still rests on a narrow group of large industrial stocks, and the market's next test will be whether gains broaden once Dangote Refinery's shares begin trading.

stories.h: Nigerian banks earn N522bn from electronic banking and card fees in 9M 2026
stories.e: Nigeria's banks collectively generated N522 billion in income from electronic banking services and card-related fees in the first nine months of 2026. The figure highlights how digital transaction charges have become an increasingly significant revenue stream for lenders.

stories.h: S&P says Nigeria's 2029 investment-grade target may be too ambitious
stories.e: S&P Global Ratings has cast doubt on Nigeria's target of regaining investment-grade credit status by 2029, saying no sovereign has historically moved from a single-B rating to investment grade within just three years. An S&P research director for Africa said sustained reform matters more than hitting a fixed timeline, even while acknowledging recent progress that led to Nigeria's first ratings upgrade since 2012.

stories.h: Naira slides to N1,445/$ in parallel market as gap with official rate widens
stories.e: The naira weakened to N1,445 to the dollar in the parallel market, widening the gap with the official exchange rate to N86.50. The depreciation highlights continuing pressure on the currency despite the Central Bank's recent efforts to narrow the spread between the two markets.

stories.h: Investors pour ₦1.08trn into 364-day treasury bill, nearly doubling target offer
stories.e: Nigerian investors subscribed ₦1.08 trillion to the latest 364-day Nigerian Treasury Bill auction, about 180 per cent of the ₦600 billion the government had offered. The strong demand reflects continued investor appetite for short-term government debt amid high interest rates and a cautious lending environment among commercial banks. The result mirrors a wider pattern in which savers and institutions have favoured government securities over riskier assets this year.

stories.h: Banks' ₦55.7trn loan book grows slowly despite recapitalisation drive
stories.e: Loans and advances at eight major Nigerian banks rose by only 2.4 per cent to ₦55.66 trillion in the nine months to September, even after the industry's recapitalisation exercise raised a combined ₦4.65 trillion. Analysts say lenders remain cautious about extending credit in a high interest-rate environment and continue to favour government securities over loans to businesses. Customer deposits grew faster than lending, pushing the industry's loan-to-deposit ratio down to about 37.2 per cent.

stories.h: CBN reforms driving faster growth in African cross-border payments, says PAPSS
stories.e: A deputy chief executive of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System, John Sebabi, said regulatory easing by the Central Bank of Nigeria, including the removal of extra documentation for smaller PAPSS transactions, has helped push transaction volumes on the platform up by roughly 1,000 per cent this year. PAPSS, now active in 32 countries with over 280 participating banks, says it has cut cross-border payment costs by 85 to 90 per cent and reduced processing times to under two minutes. The platform's progress will be reviewed at a forum in Addis Ababa later this month.

stories.h: Naira suffers biggest single-day loss since October as it slips to N1,364/$
stories.e: The naira closed at N1,364 to the dollar on the official market on 11 November, down from N1,353.50 the previous session in its steepest single-day fall since 22 October, a 0.78 per cent depreciation. The currency remains stronger than its N1,431/$ close at the start of 2026, though foreign reserves grew by just $295.35 million in October, the slowest monthly gain this year. The parallel market quoted the naira even weaker, at around N1,430/$.

stories.h: Afreximbank commits $75m to Development Bank of Nigeria for SME lending
stories.e: The African Export-Import Bank has agreed to channel $75 million through the Development Bank of Nigeria to expand financing for small and medium-sized enterprises. The facility is intended to ease the credit squeeze facing Nigerian SMEs, which continue to struggle with high borrowing costs despite recent central bank interventions.

stories.h: Sterlings Alternative Bank appoints Gul Khan as managing director
stories.e: Sterling Financial Holdings has appointed banking executive Gul Khan, formerly chief executive of Kenyas I&M Bank, as managing director of its non-interest subsidiary, Alternative Bank, with Central Bank of Nigeria approval. He succeeds Hassan Yusuf, whose tenure ended on 4 November, and is expected to drive the banks digital expansion.

stories.h: States must contribute to N400bn fund to access minimum pension scheme, says PenCom
stories.e: The National Pension Commission has said state governments must contribute to a N400 billion fund before they can benefit from the minimum pension guarantee scheme for retirees. The requirement is intended to ensure states share the financial responsibility for pension obligations rather than relying solely on federal backing.

stories.h: CBN allots N3.854 trillion in OMO auction, far exceeding original offer
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria allotted N3.854 trillion in its latest Open Market Operations auction, more than N2.354 trillion above the amount initially offered, as it worked to mop up excess liquidity in the banking system. The scale of the oversubscription signals strong demand from banks for short-term, high-yielding instruments.

stories.h: CBN overhauls Agricultural Credit Guarantee Scheme to draw in private capital
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria is overhauling its nearly 50-year-old Agricultural Credit Guarantee Scheme Fund, unveiling a new operational framework, an online portal and partnership agreements meant to mobilise private and commercial finance into farming. Governor Olayemi Cardoso told a stakeholder roundtable in Abuja that the goal was to "crowd private capital in, not crowd it out," as the scheme shifts from simply guaranteeing loans towards coordinating wider agricultural investment.

stories.h: CBN digitalises fiscal data collection across 36 states, FCT and 774 LGAs
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria is rolling out a digital platform to replace its largely manual twice-yearly Sub-National Fiscal Survey, aiming for more accurate, timely and traceable public finance data from every state, the FCT and all 774 local government areas. Training began in late October and is due to finish by early December, with sixteen states already covered and attendance near 100 per cent at sessions held so far. The initiative, which supports a shift to quarterly reporting, follows a September memorandum formalising fiscal and monetary policy coordination between the federal government and the central bank.

stories.h: CBN opens N1.5trn OMO auction as banking-system cash exceeds N5.9trn
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria opened a N1.5 trillion Open Market Operations auction, its third in a week, as banking-system liquidity climbed above N5.9 trillion and the Financial Market Dealers Association reported system liquidity up 15.36 per cent week-on-week to N8.5 trillion. The CBN has already raised roughly N5.67 trillion through OMO sales since 3 November, about 92 per cent of October's total allotment, as it continues mopping up excess naira liquidity. The Debt Management Office is also running a separate N800 billion treasury bill auction this week.

stories.h: CBN digitalises sub-national economic survey across states, FCT and LGAs
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria has moved its periodic sub-national economic survey onto a digital platform, extending the exercise to all 36 states, the FCT and local government areas. Officials say the shift is meant to speed up data collection and improve the accuracy of regional economic statistics used for policy planning. The initiative is part of the CBN broader push to modernise how it gathers information on economic activity outside the federal level.

stories.h: Dangote Refinery IPO draws about ₦5.85trn in share applications
stories.e: Demand for shares in the Dangote Petroleum Refinery initial public offering has come in at around ₦5.85 trillion, nearly three times the size of the original offer, according to Bloomberg-sourced figures reported by BusinessDay. The scale of subscription underlines strong investor appetite for the refinery despite broader economic headwinds in Nigeria. Final allotment decisions are expected once the exchange and regulators complete their review of the offer.

stories.h: CBN returns N2.87 trillion to banks but borrowing costs stay high
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria has returned N2.87 trillion in funds to commercial banks, yet interbank borrowing costs have remained elevated, suggesting persistent liquidity tightness in the banking system. The move comes alongside a fresh N1.5 trillion open market operations auction as system cash levels exceeded N5.9 trillion.

stories.h: Nigeria's FX market turnover plunges 51% to $1.81bn in a week
stories.e: Dollar turnover on Nigeria's official foreign exchange market fell by more than half week-on-week to about $1.81 billion, its steepest weekly drop of 2026, even as the naira held broadly stable near ₦1,349 to the dollar. Analysts linked the slowdown to reduced spot and forward trading activity, while attention turns to this month's inflation data and the Central Bank's next interest rate decision.

stories.h: Access Holdings weighs exit from foreign unit to meet CBN subsidiary investment cap
stories.e: Access Holdings says it may sell at least one foreign subsidiary after the Central Bank of Nigeria found its overseas investments equalled about 19.3 per cent of shareholders' funds, nearly double the 10 per cent ceiling set under the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act. The lender has 12 months to comply and is also considering recalling surplus capital from some units and restructuring others.

stories.h: Rising energy costs drain N820.7bn from NGX-listed industrial firms
stories.e: Industrial goods companies listed on the Nigerian Exchange spent roughly N820.7 billion on fuel and power in the first nine months of 2026, a 6.3 per cent rise year-on-year that is squeezing profit margins. Cement producers Dangote and BUA account for the bulk of that spending, reflecting continued reliance on self-generated power due to an unreliable national grid. Analysts warn manufacturers are struggling to pass these rising costs on to customers.

stories.h: NUPRC approves 595 well re-entries and 145 new drilling operations as rig count hits 100
stories.e: Nigeria's upstream petroleum regulator, the NUPRC, said it has approved 595 well re-entries and 145 new drilling operations, pushing the country's active rig count to 100 for the first time in years. The commission described the increase as evidence of renewed investor confidence in Nigeria's oil and gas sector following recent reforms. A higher rig count typically signals increased future production and could support government revenue projections tied to oil output.

stories.h: Nigerian industrial goods firms' tax payments surge 99% under new tax law
stories.e: Seven listed Nigerian industrial goods companies, including Dangote Cement, BUA Cement and Beta Glass, paid a combined N271.7 billion in income tax in the first nine months of 2026, almost double the same period last year, as Nigeria's new tax framework took effect from January 2026. Combined pre-tax profit across the group rose 43 per cent to N2.49 trillion, though Dangote Cement's own tax bill fell even as its profit grew.

stories.h: Nigeria to start local production of pharmaceutical ingredients by Q1 2027, FG says
stories.e: The Federal Government says Nigeria will begin manufacturing active pharmaceutical ingredients locally from the first quarter of 2027, with a major pharmaceutical company set to build the production plant. PVAC National Coordinator Mukhtar Abdul announced the plan at the 2026 Joint Annual Review in Abuja, framing it as a move to cut reliance on imports. A 2026 KPMG report found that roughly nine in ten active ingredients and excipients used by Nigerian drug makers are currently imported.

stories.h: Nigerian Breweries, Nestle Nigeria and peers book N129.4bn in fees to foreign parents
stories.e: Nigerian Breweries, Nestle Nigeria and several other consumer goods manufacturers paid a combined N129.4 billion in fees and royalties to their foreign parent companies, according to newly reviewed financial filings. The figures renew questions about how much value locally listed manufacturers retain domestically versus what flows abroad.

stories.h: Dangote Cement suspends proposed London Stock Exchange listing
stories.e: Dangote Cement has put on hold its proposed secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange, citing current market conditions and strategic priorities, after earlier signalling in May and July that London was its preferred venue over Dubai for broadening access to overseas investors. The company said its shares remain listed on the Nigerian Exchange and that the decision does not affect its operations, which span 55 million tonnes of annual production capacity across eleven African countries. Dangote Cement, majority-owned by Aliko Dangote, reported a 31 per cent rise in nine-month profit and revenue of N3.8 trillion.

stories.h: Dangote Cement shelves planned London Stock Exchange listing
stories.e: Dangote Cement has called off its previously announced plan to pursue a secondary listing on the London Stock Exchange, according to BusinessDay. The company has not given detailed public reasons for the reversal, though the move comes amid wider volatility in Nigerian capital markets and corporate listing plans. Dangote Cement remains Nigeria dominant cement producer and a bellwether for the country manufacturing sector.

stories.h: Nigeria's solar panel assembly capacity set to double by 2031 - IEA
stories.e: The International Energy Agency projects that Nigeria will at least double its local solar panel assembly capacity, from roughly 500 megawatts a year currently to more than one gigawatt annually by 2031. The agency cautioned that these early-stage manufacturing ventures are unlikely to significantly reduce Nigeria's heavy reliance on imported solar components within that timeframe.

stories.h: FG unveils plans for three lithium processing factories to cut battery imports
stories.e: Vice-President Kashim Shettima says the federal government plans to build three lithium processing factories, in Nasarawa, Kaduna and Abuja, to help Nigeria move up the critical minerals and battery manufacturing value chain and reduce reliance on imported batteries. He made the announcement at an international conference on the African Continental Free Trade Area, though no investment figures or timeline were given.

stories.h: Why Nigeria's cassava output still fails to feed its factories
stories.e: Despite being the world's largest cassava producer, Nigeria's processors continue to face feedstock shortages, according to findings discussed at an industry roundtable. The gap is attributed to overstated national output figures, low farm yields, high harvesting and transport costs, and the marketing of cheaper derivatives as substitutes for genuine cassava starch. Industry voices say solving the supply, cost and demand problems together is essential to unlocking the crop's industrial potential.

stories.h: Indorama commits $261m to a fourth fertiliser production line in Nigeria
stories.e: Indorama has issued a letter of award to South Korea's Daewoo for a new $261 million ammonia-urea line at its Eleme complex near Port Harcourt, a project that would lift the company's installed Nigerian urea capacity by about a third. The expansion comes as Gulf shipping disruptions have pushed global urea prices to multi-year highs.

stories.h: Dangote Cement, BUA spend N797 billion in energy cost
stories.e: Nigeria's two largest cement makers, Dangote Cement and BUA Cement, spent a combined N797.1 billion on fuel and power in the first nine months of 2026, nearly 7% more than a year earlier, as both firms leaned on self-generated electricity to cope with a national grid that failed repeatedly during the year. BUA's energy bill rose more than 21%, far outpacing Dangote's smaller 2% increase.

stories.h: BUA Cement, Nigerian Breweries among firms quitting the national grid for private power
stories.e: Regulatory filings show BUA Cement, Nigerian Breweries and several other manufacturers and public institutions secured permits for nearly 55 megawatts of captive power generation in the first half of 2026, as repeated grid collapses push major electricity users to go it alone. The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria says its members' spending on alternative power rose more than 20% to over ₦1.3 trillion in 2025, and analysts warn the exodus of big customers could further strain the national grid's finances.

stories.h: Dangote Launches $2.5bn Fuel Storage and Pipeline Project in Namibia
stories.e: Aliko Dangote has broken ground on a $2.5 billion fuel storage and pipeline project near Namibia's Walvis Bay port, targeting landlocked southern African markets that rely on imported petroleum. The facility will include roughly four million barrels of storage capacity and is tied to a proposed 1,700-kilometre pipeline linking Namibia to Botswana and South Africa.

stories.h: Nigeria's biggest firms hit by fourfold surge in energy costs
stories.e: Nigeria's largest listed companies spent nearly four times more on energy in the first half of 2026 compared with a year earlier, driven by rising fuel prices. The surge adds pressure to manufacturers' already tight margins and raises fresh concerns about the cost of doing business in Nigeria's industrial sector.

stories.h: BUA Foods posts 11% profit growth despite falling revenue
stories.e: BUA Foods reported an 11% rise in nine-month profit to N450.47 billion even as revenue fell 19% to N1.15 trillion amid weaker consumer demand and lower prices. The company credited cost management and productivity gains for widening its profit margin despite softer sales.

stories.h: Dangote weighs up to $15bn refining and petrochemicals investment in Egypt
stories.e: Aliko Dangote is in talks with Egyptian officials over a potential $10-15 billion investment focused on oil refining and petrochemicals, aimed at turning Egypt from a fuel importer into a net exporter. The discussions followed a visit to Dangote's Lagos headquarters by Egypt's investment minister, and the final scale of the deal is still being negotiated.

stories.h: Beta Glass's nine-month profit falls 8% as finance costs and FX losses bite
stories.e: Packaging manufacturer Beta Glass saw after-tax profit slip 8.4% to N24.93 billion for the nine months to September, even though revenue rose nearly 5%, as finance costs jumped 45% and the company swung to a foreign-exchange loss. Nairametrics notes the company's third-quarter profit actually grew on its own, showing the annual decline was driven mainly by earlier-year pressures.

stories.h: Manufacturing credit falls 34% despite N4.65trn bank recapitalisation, economists warn
stories.e: New figures presented at a Lagos banking event show credit to Nigerian manufacturers has dropped by about a third since December 2024, even as lenders raised N4.65 trillion in fresh capital, with banks instead favouring oil and gas, trade and government securities. Economic analysts are calling for a coordinated financing framework, warning that industrial growth is being starved of credit despite stronger bank balance sheets.

stories.h: Nigeria's top cement makers post combined N1.71trn profit in nine months
stories.e: Nigeria's three major cement producers posted a combined 37.8% rise in nine-month profit to N1.71 trillion, driven largely by stronger margins and cost efficiencies rather than higher sales volumes. The results underline the sector's continued profitability even as high construction costs remain a strain on ordinary Nigerians.

stories.h: Malaysia detains 59 foreigners in raids linked to Nigerian's deadly machete attack
stories.e: Malaysian immigration officers arrested 59 foreign nationals in raids on business premises in Selangor, a day after a machete attack on police officers in Kepong in which the suspect, reported by local media to be Nigerian, was shot dead by police. Authorities said the raids followed two weeks of intelligence gathering rather than being a direct response to the attack, and did not disclose the nationalities of those detained. Separately, Malaysia's immigration chief said Nigerians accounted for the largest number of African nationals, 53 of 112, arrested for immigration offences between January and October 2026.

stories.h: Gunmen abduct graduate, three others in Ogun, demand N500m ransom
stories.e: Armed kidnappers seized a recent graduate and three other people in Ogun State and are demanding a N500 million ransom for their release. The abduction adds to a continuing wave of kidnapping-for-ransom incidents affecting south-western Nigeria.

stories.h: Thugs attack NDC supporters, disrupt Peter Obi's Lagos town hall
stories.e: Suspected thugs armed with cutlasses and clubs stormed a Nigeria Democratic Congress town hall for presidential candidate Peter Obi in Oregun, Ikeja, forcing attendees to flee before supporters repelled the attackers. The assault is the latest in a string of attacks on opposition political gatherings across several states in recent weeks, raising fresh concern over political violence ahead of 2027.

stories.h: Plateau lifts curfew in Barkin Ladi, Bokkos and Mangu
stories.e: Plateau State has lifted the dusk-to-dawn curfew it had imposed on Barkin Ladi, Bokkos and Mangu local government areas following a spate of deadly attacks. The restriction had curtailed residents' movement for weeks as authorities worked to restore security in the affected communities.

stories.h: Amnesty condemns attack on PDP candidate Pantamis convoy in Gombe
stories.e: Amnesty International has condemned an attack in which armed thugs blocked a highway with burning tyres and smashed vehicle windscreens in an attempt to stop PDP governorship candidate Isa Pantamis convoy from reaching Gombe. The rights group said preliminary findings point to possible links with the ruling APC and criticised the apparent absence of arrests, urging a thorough investigation.

stories.h: Press groups condemn remand of FIJ journalist Daniel Ojukwu
stories.e: Daniel Ojukwu, a reporter with the Foundation for Investigative Journalism, has been remanded in Kuje Correctional Centre for 21 days after being arraigned on cybercrime and defamation charges linked to his reporting on an official government office. Press freedom groups, including CPJ and the Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism, have condemned the remand and called for his release, warning of a chilling effect on reporting ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.h: Reps resolve to probe Nigerias alarming rise in human trafficking
stories.e: The House of Representatives has resolved to investigate the growing scale of human trafficking in Nigeria, following a motion by Dominic Okafor of Anambra State. Lawmakers urged stronger enforcement, prosecution of traffickers and better support for victims, particularly women and children, and gave relevant committees four weeks to report on the patterns and drivers of trafficking, including poverty and displacement.

stories.h: UNHCR appeals for $2m as over 66,000 flee Nigeria violence into Niger, Benin
stories.e: The UN refugee agency says violence in northern Nigeria has driven more than 66,000 people into Niger and Benin since the start of the year, nearly three times last years figure for the same period. UNHCR is appealing for $2 million to register new arrivals and provide identity documents and assistance between November 2026 and January 2027, warning that tens of thousands remain unregistered because of funding shortfalls.

stories.h: Violence in northern Nigeria drives nearly 64,000 people into Niger, says UNHCR
stories.e: The UN refugee agency says almost 64,000 people have fled attacks by Boko Haram, ISWAP and armed criminal gangs in northern Nigeria into Niger this year, with the Diffa region bearing most of the strain. UNHCR warns that only a small fraction of new arrivals have been formally registered and that humanitarian funding is falling well short of what is needed.

stories.h: Reps to investigate rising human trafficking cases and trafficking syndicates
stories.e: Nigerias House of Representatives has ordered its Human Rights, Interior and Police Affairs committees to spend four weeks investigating the scale of human trafficking, including forced labour, domestic servitude and organ harvesting. Lawmakers linked the rise to poverty and insecurity, and urged NAPTIP to strengthen surveillance against cross-border trafficking networks.

stories.h: Rights groups demand release of FIJ journalist Daniel Ojukwu from Kuje Prison
stories.e: Press freedom and civil society groups are demanding the release of Daniel Ojukwu, a journalist with the Foundation for Investigative Journalism, who remains held at Kuje Prison over his reporting on a former presidential aide. Campaigners say his continued detention reflects a wider pattern of using the justice system to silence journalists covering official wrongdoing.

stories.h: Amnesty International urges oil firms to fund Niger Delta environmental clean-up
stories.e: Amnesty International has called on oil companies operating in the Niger Delta to fund the long-delayed clean-up of pollution affecting local communities, saying years of promises have not translated into visible remediation. The group argued that firms profiting from the region's resources bear a direct responsibility for repairing the environmental damage.

stories.h: US Congress to examine Nigeria's response to Christian killings, Middle Belt insecurity
stories.e: The US House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Africa, chaired by Chris Smith, is to hold a hearing titled One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria's Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt, examining extremist violence and Nigerian government efforts to protect affected communities. Witnesses are expected to include State Department officials alongside representatives of the Hudson Institute, Open Doors US and CSIS, in what will be Smith's fourteenth hearing on the subject. The session follows Nigeria's 2025 redesignation as a Country of Particular Concern and precedes continuing US-Nigeria counterterrorism cooperation in the north.

stories.h: NHRC records 384,196 human rights violation complaints in October, up 13.4%
stories.e: The National Human Rights Commission logged 384,196 complaints of rights violations in October, a 13.4 per cent rise on September's 338,810, with discrimination the largest category at 217,243 cases, around 180,000 of them from internally displaced persons' camps. Executive Secretary Tony Ojukwu said every complaint represents a person, a family, or a community whose rights and dignity need protection, while officials noted Lagos and Rivers entered the top ten states for the first time this year, linked partly to pre-election tension. The commission said it resolved 1,455 cases and visited 108 detention facilities during the month.

stories.h: After decades of unanswered complaints, Akwa Ibom communities learn to document oil pollution
stories.e: Farmers and residents in Akwa Ibom's Ikono and Ibiono Ibom council areas are being trained to systematically gather evidence of pollution from ageing and abandoned oil wells, after decades of complaints to oil companies and regulators produced little action. Organisers say better-documented evidence, including photographs and location data, could strengthen communities' case for remediation and compensation.

stories.h: Court rejects Sowore bid to subpoena DSS lawyer in cyberbullying trial
stories.e: A Federal High Court in Abuja has turned down activist Omoyele Sowore request to subpoena the Department of State Services lead counsel as a defence witness in his long-running cyberbullying trial. The DSS had argued the subpoena was improper and amounted to an abuse of court process. The ruling is the latest setback in a case that has dragged through multiple procedural disputes since Sowore was charged over comments about President Tinubu.

stories.h: Bandits burn 12 family members to death in Zamfara attack
stories.e: Gunmen attacked Gidan Taba village in Maradun local government area of Zamfara State on Saturday night, setting fire to a room and killing 12 members of one family, according to residents and the local council chairman. Police put the toll at 11 dead, while seven other residents were reportedly abducted during the raid. The attack adds to a string of deadly banditry incidents that have continued to afflict communities across the state.

stories.h: Twelve members of one family killed in Zamfara bandit attack
stories.e: Suspected bandits set fire to a room sheltering a family in Gidan Taba village, Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State, killing twelve people including a father, his wives and young children, according to the council chairman. Local vigilantes repelled the attackers and rescued some captives, while police say security operatives are pursuing the perpetrators; other outlets have put the toll at eleven or thirteen.

stories.h: 'Don't bring your camera': Lagos street gangs extort filmmakers
stories.e: Al Jazeera reports that filmmakers, photographers and journalists working in Lagos face routine threats and extortion demands from street touts known as agberos, with one crew member stabbed during a dispute over payment in Ajah. Lagos State's Commissioner for Information says no one has authority to demand such payments and that police will handle complaints, but analysts warn the harassment is pushing productions off the streets and could lead journalists to under-report sensitive events.

stories.h: Filmmakers and journalists in Lagos describe rising extortion by street touts
stories.e: Filmmakers, photographers and journalists working in Lagos say they are increasingly being stopped by groups of touts, or agberos, demanding payment before they are allowed to keep filming in public, with several reporting threats, assaults and damage to equipment when they refused. A Lagos state government spokesperson said no one has the authority to demand money from people filming in public and that such cases would be referred to the police, though analysts warn the harassment is already raising production costs and discouraging coverage of sensitive stories.

stories.h: Fani-Kayode presents credentials to Ramaphosa, begins duty as envoy to South Africa
stories.e: Femi Fani-Kayode formally began his assignment as Nigeria's High Commissioner to South Africa, presenting his Letter of Credence to President Cyril Ramaphosa in Pretoria alongside envoys from 14 other countries. He invoked Nigeria's support for South Africa during the anti-apartheid era and said his task was to reset bilateral ties, but complained that South African state media had livestreamed every other new ambassador's remarks except his. The ceremony comes amid persistent strain between the two countries over xenophobic violence against Nigerian migrants, with Fani-Kayode previously estimating that South African police have killed at least 30 Nigerians over the past four years.

stories.h: Nigeria and EU sign deal to facilitate return of irregular migrants
stories.e: Nigeria and the European Union have signed an agreement intended to make it easier to return Nigerians living in Europe without valid immigration status. The deal forms part of broader migration cooperation between Abuja and Brussels.

stories.h: Nigeria fields third-largest delegation among nations at COP31 climate summit
stories.e: Nigeria sent the third-largest national delegation to the COP31 climate summit, a record gathering that is drawing global attention to Africa's role in climate negotiations. The scale of Nigeria's presence reflects the country's push to secure climate financing and shape outcomes relevant to Africa, including adaptation funding and the energy transition. Separately at the summit, African youth delegates presented a mapping of water challenges across 51 countries, calling for a greater role in policy decisions.

stories.h: AfDB and AFD sign five-year deal to expand African infrastructure financing
stories.e: The African Development Bank Group and France's Agence Francaise de Developpement signed a memorandum of understanding on the sidelines of the Paris Peace Forum, extending their partnership on jointly financed infrastructure projects across 14 African countries, including Nigeria, through 2031. The deal covers energy, transport, water, agriculture and digital infrastructure, building on 17 projects the two institutions have already co-financed since 2021.

stories.h: Nigeria pitches $2.2bn flare gas capture plan to investors at COP31
stories.e: At a side event at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission chief executive Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan pitched a $2.2 billion flare gas capture programme to international investors, aimed at ending routine gas flaring at Nigerian oil fields. The event also launched a new emissions-tracking portal, even as official data show the share of gas flared in Nigeria rose in August to its highest level since October 2025.

stories.h: Amnesty says UN and South Sudan officials failed to stop village massacre
stories.e: Amnesty International has accused United Nations and South Sudanese officials of failing to act on warnings that could have prevented a deadly massacre in a South Sudanese village. The finding adds to mounting criticism of the international communitys response to recurring violence in the country.

stories.h: Nigerian environmental group urges COP31 negotiators to commit to binding fossil fuel phase-out
stories.e: The Health of Mother Earth Foundation is pressing negotiators at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, to agree a binding, transparent pathway away from coal, oil and gas rather than relying on voluntary pledges. The group warns some fossil-fuel-producing nations are trying to strip language requiring that shift from the text, and argues a proposed electrification target would offer little climate benefit if the extra power still comes from fossil sources. HOMEF is also calling for climate finance to be delivered as grants rather than loans, warning that the window to act before the 2028 global stocktake is narrowing.

stories.h: COP31: climate activists reject carbon capture and marine geoengineering as false solutions
stories.e: Campaigners from the Indigenous Environmental Network and allied groups used a COP31 demonstration in Turkey to dismiss carbon capture technology and marine geoengineering as distractions that let polluting industries avoid cutting emissions. They argued that wealthier nations and corporations are promoting these approaches to delay more meaningful climate action, at the expense of the Global South.

stories.h: US House committee to review Nigeria's response to attacks on Christians
stories.e: A committee of the United States House of Representatives is to review Nigeria's handling of attacks on Christian communities, amid continued debate in Washington over how the Nigerian government has responded to sectarian and communal violence. The review follows pressure from US lawmakers who have repeatedly raised the issue in Congress.

stories.h: UN warns petrol and food prices rising globally as Iran war worsens El Nino impact
stories.e: The United Nations says petrol and food prices are climbing worldwide as the war involving Iran compounds the economic effects of El Nino-related weather disruption, with Nigeria among the countries exposed to the knock-on effects. The warning adds to concerns about affordability pressures already facing Nigerian households.

stories.h: US Congressman who alleged Christian genocide in Nigeria wins re-election
stories.e: Republican Congressman Riley Moore, one of the most vocal promoters in Washington of claims that Christians are facing genocide in Nigeria, has won re-election to the US House with just under 60 per cent of the vote. His claims remain contested, with some US lawmakers warning against oversimplified narratives and independent media investigations finding much of the underlying data cannot be verified.

stories.h: COP31 climate talks open in Antalya amid finance dispute and calls to get serious
stories.e: The COP31 United Nations climate conference opened in Antalya, Turkey, with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urging world leaders to get serious about cutting emissions. The ceremony was delayed by around ninety minutes amid a dispute over whether climate finance would feature on the formal agenda, a standoff that was eventually resolved partly in favour of developing countries. The outcome will be closely watched by African and other Global South delegations seeking stronger commitments on climate finance.

stories.h: African nations to press for climate finance commitments at COP31
stories.e: Negotiators representing Africas 54 nations say they will push for predictable, grant-based climate finance and a full replenishment of the Green Climate Fund when COP31 opens in Antalya, Turkiye. The African Group of Negotiators, which includes Nigerias delegation, insists wealthier nations must meet their existing Paris Agreement obligations before any new financing contributors are brought in, and wants a broader, more equitable approach to the global shift away from fossil fuels.

stories.h: WHO: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak is now the largest ever recorded there
stories.e: The World Health Organisation says the Ebola outbreak centred on Ituri and North Kivu provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the largest the country has ever recorded, with over 10,600 confirmed cases and more than 5,100 deaths as of early November. Nigeria is among five countries to have recorded a case, after a patient diagnosed in Abuja in October was evacuated to Switzerland for treatment.

stories.h: WHO backs trials of two new vaccines against DRC's deadly Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak
stories.e: The World Health Organization's vaccine advisory group has recommended two additional candidate vaccines, Oxford/Serum Institute's ChAdOx1 and Moderna's mRNA-1469, for testing against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola during the Democratic Republic of Congo's ongoing outbreak. It marks the first time vaccines designed specifically for this Ebola strain have been trialled during an active outbreak, with results expected in early 2027. The WHO has also urged countries not to impose travel restrictions on people from the DRC in response to the outbreak.

stories.h: US lawmaker who accused USAID of funding Boko Haram loses re-election bid
stories.e: Pennsylvania Republican Scott Perry, who in 2025 told Congress without evidence that USAID had funnelled money to Boko Haram and other terrorist groups, lost his House seat in the November 3 midterms to Democrat Janelle Stelson. Nigerian officials and a Nigerian lawyer had previously pushed back on the unsubstantiated claim, which a former US ambassador to Nigeria also rejected.

stories.h: 14 Nigerian-Americans win state and local races in US midterm elections
stories.e: Abike Dabiri-Erewa, chair of Nigeria's diaspora commission, says 14 Nigerian-Americans won seats across the United States in Tuesday's midterms, including state legislature wins in Georgia, Texas, Ohio, Minnesota and Michigan, plus Will Jawando's election as Montgomery County executive in Maryland. The wins add to a growing number of Nigerian-Americans holding elected office across multiple US states.

stories.h: World Bank raises alarm as developing countries' external debt hits record $9.4 trillion
stories.e: The World Bank's newly released International Debt Report found that developing countries' external debt hit a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, growing at its fastest pace since 2021 as governments leaned more heavily on private creditors and bond markets. The report singles out Nigeria, noting its external debt stock climbed to $54.52 billion by mid-2026 and that the country spent $5.21 billion servicing external debt last year.

stories.h: Nigerian-born scholar Dapo Akande elected judge of the International Court of Justice
stories.e: Dapo Akande, a Nigerian-born Oxford professor of international law running as the United Kingdom's candidate, has been elected to a nine-year term on the International Court of Justice, the UN's top judicial body. He will take his seat on the Hague-based court in February 2027. His election highlights the continued influence of Nigerian-trained legal scholars within major international institutions.

stories.h: Mo Ibrahim warns Africa is backsliding into a 'strongman' era
stories.e: Sudanese-British billionaire Mo Ibrahim says the continent's governance gains have stalled and that authoritarian 'strongmen' are resurging, tying the trend to a broader global drift away from democratic norms. He pointed to his foundation's governance index, which he says shows little improvement across much of Africa in recent years, as a warning sign for citizens and policymakers alike.

stories.h: Super Eagles beat Tanzania 3-1 to revive AFCON qualifying hopes
stories.e: Nigeria's Super Eagles beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo in their Group L qualifier for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, with a brace from Tolu Arokodare and a goal from Alhassan Yusuf. The win was described as crucial after Nigeria's qualifying campaign was dented by a 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau in their previous match, leaving the team needing results to keep pace with the group's leaders. Tanzania had already secured a place at the 2027 tournament as a co-host alongside Kenya and Uganda, so the result mattered chiefly for Nigeria's own qualification hopes.

stories.h: Super Eagles seek redemption against Tanzania in Uyo AFCON qualifier
stories.e: Nigeria's Super Eagles face Tanzania in Uyo in a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, looking to bounce back after their recent defeat to Guinea-Bissau. Coach Eric Chelle said the team is focused solely on securing victory to keep their qualification hopes on track.

stories.h: Flamingos' Umejiaku says FIFA U-17 World Cup best player award was a first
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos midfielder Oluebube Umejiaku said winning the best player award at the 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup was the first individual honour of her career. The award adds to a strong showing by Nigeria's youth teams on the global stage this year.

stories.h: Tinubu rewards Flamingos with ₦100m savings bonds each after historic World Cup win
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu approved a ₦100 million federal savings bond for every member of the Flamingos, Nigeria's under-17 women's team, after they became the first African side to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup. Head coach Busari Hakeem Ishola will receive ₦100 million in cash, while other technical staff get ₦50 million each. The team beat Japan 2-1 in the final after recovering from an opening defeat to Poland, winning six matches in a row to lift the trophy.

stories.h: Super Eagles full 24-man squad assembles in Uyo for Tanzania qualifier
stories.e: All 24 invited Super Eagles players, including Alex Iwobi, Ademola Lookman and Wilfred Ndidi, have arrived in camp in Uyo ahead of a must-win 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Tanzania. The early assembly is intended to give the coaching staff extra time to work on tactics and match fitness before Fridays game.

stories.h: Tinubu rewards Flamingos with N100m savings bonds after historic World Cup win
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has rewarded Nigerias U-17 womens team with a N100 million Federal Government savings bond for each player, after they became the first African side to win the FIFA U-17 Womens World Cup. Head coach Busari Hakeem Ishola received N100 million in cash and the rest of the technical crew N50 million each, with the award unveiled by First Lady Oluremi Tinubu.

stories.h: Tinubu rewards Flamingos with N100 million each for World Cup victory
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has announced a reward of N100 million for each member of the Flamingos after the team won Nigeria's first FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title. The gesture follows weeks of public debate over how the government and football officials engaged with the squad during and after the tournament.

stories.h: Senate pledges N100m reward for Flamingos after World Cup triumph
stories.e: Nigeria's Senate has pledged a N100 million reward for the Flamingos, the country's victorious under-17 women's football team, after they became the first African side to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup. The team beat Japan in the final in Morocco, capping a tournament in which they recovered from an opening defeat to lift the trophy.

stories.h: Flamingos arrive home in Abuja as FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup champions
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos touched down in Abuja to a hero's welcome after becoming the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, beating Japan 2-1 in the final despite having lost their opening group match. The team has since been showered with cash rewards, and President Bola Tinubu has directed the National Sports Commission to clear all outstanding bonuses owed to the players and officials.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos crowned first African champions of FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 in the final in Morocco to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, becoming the first African side, men's or women's, to lift the trophy. The team recovered from an opening defeat to Poland and knocked out defending champions North Korea en route to the final. President Bola Tinubu, the First Lady and CAF President Patrice Motsepe were among those who congratulated the squad.

stories.h: Flamingos crowned world champions, return home to Abuja reception
stories.e: Nigeria's under-17 women's football team, the Flamingos, arrived back in Abuja to a warm reception after being crowned world champions, having beaten Japan 2-1 in the final of the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco. The victory marks Nigeria's first title at this level, surpassing the squad's previous best finish of third place.

stories.h: Nwankwo and Bright win Nigeria's first two golds at Dakar Youth Olympics
stories.e: Rosemary Nwankwo and Gift Bright won Nigeria's first two gold medals at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, taking the girls' and boys' 100m sprint titles respectively. Bright's personal-best run made him the first Nigerian to win the boys' 100m crown at the Youth Olympics, lifting the country to joint 14th on the medal table alongside Ecuador as the Games continue in Senegal.

stories.h: Flamingos become first African side to win FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 in Rabat, Morocco, to become the first African team to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, with midfielder Oluebube Umejiaku named the tournament's best player. President Bola Tinubu congratulated the squad and coaching staff, calling the victory a source of pride for the country, as the team's run through the tournament drew widespread celebration across Nigeria.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos beat Japan to win first-ever FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos defeated Japan 2-1 in Rabat, Morocco to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, becoming the first African team ever to claim the title. Goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku secured the win after the side recovered from an opening defeat to Poland to post six consecutive victories through the knockout rounds.

stories.h: Flamingos make history, beat Japan to win Nigerias first U-17 Womens World Cup
stories.e: Nigerias Flamingos defeated Japan to claim the countrys first-ever FIFA U-17 Womens World Cup title, a landmark achievement for Nigerian womens football celebrated by officials and fans nationwide. Senate President Godswill Akpabio and other public figures congratulated the team, with coach Fatai Busari crediting the win to years of sustained development work rather than a one-off success.

stories.h: Flamingos beat Japan 2-1 to win Nigeria's first FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's football team, the Flamingos, defeated Japan 2-1 in Morocco to win the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final, becoming the first African side to lift the trophy. Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku scored for Nigeria, with Fuki Ito replying for Japan, capping a run in which the Flamingos recovered from an opening defeat to Poland to win five successive matches.

stories.h: Flamingos chase Nigeria's first FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title against Japan
stories.e: Nigeria's Flamingos face Japan in Rabat on Saturday evening, seeking a historic first FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup title after beating Brazil 3-1 in the semi-final to reach their first-ever final. Japan reached the final by edging North Korea 4-1 on penalties after a 1-1 draw. A Nigerian win would make it the first African country to hold FIFA titles in both the men's and women's U-17 categories.

stories.h: Nigeria's Flamingos face Japan in U-17 Women's World Cup final, chasing Africa's first title
stories.e: Nigeria's U-17 women's team has won five straight matches in Morocco to reach the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup final against Japan, including a 3-1 semi-final win over Brazil. A victory on Saturday would make Nigeria the first African nation to win the tournament, against a Japanese side chasing its second title in four final appearances.

stories.h: South Africa Leads After Day One of 2026 All Africa Challenge Trophy in Abuja
stories.e: South Africa tops the team standings after the opening round of the 2026 All Africa Challenge Trophy, a continental women's golf championship Nigeria is hosting in Abuja, with Kenya and Tanzania close behind. Host nation Nigeria sits in fifth as the tournament, which draws teams from across the continent, continues through the week.

stories.h: Cristiano Ronaldo Retires From Portugal National Team
stories.e: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football after 23 years representing Portugal, closing out a career that spanned six World Cups and the men's all-time international scoring record. The decision followed a fallout with new national coach Jorge Jesus, who had benched the veteran forward and signalled he would not start him going forward.
